expected_evidence: Geological: discrete Younger Dryas boundary (YDB) layer (~12.8 ka) in ice-core and terrestrial stratigraphy showing platinum-group-element (esp. platinum) enrichment, iridium anomaly, magnetic/glassy spherules, and nanodiamond concentrations consistent with extraterrestrial fallout.

Astronomical/cosmogenic: spikes in cosmogenic/nucleosynthetic isotopes (10Be, 36Cl, 14C, possibly 60Fe) in dated Greenland ice-core layers (GISP2, NGRIP, NEEM) indicating a pulse of extraterrestrial or cosmic-ray-derived material coincident with YD onset.
Material: embedded extraterrestrial dust/micrometeorite particles or impact-melt glass within the correlating ice-sheet firn/ice layers.

Geological (secondary, off-ice-sheet): correlating 'black mat' sediment layers and megafaunal bone beds across North America/Europe dated to the same interval, often cited in YD impact-hypothesis literature.
Genetic: megafaunal extinction/population bottleneck signals clustering near 12.9 ka (weak, indirect corroboration only).

Model-prior (low-tier, from training, not the supplied evidence set): published YDIH literature (Firestone et al. 2007 nanodiamonds; Petaev et al. 2013 Greenland platinum spike; critiques by Pigati, Holliday, van Hoesel disputing reproducibility) — this body of work centers on a cometary/asteroidal impactor, not a supernova, so the specific 'supernova-event' actor paired with 'impact-ejecta-fallout' mechanism is an unusual, less-supported variant that should be flagged as speculative.
response.rationale: The hypothesis maps most naturally onto the 'younger-dryas' period bucket given the -11000 to -10001 interval. The dominant evidence kinds implicated by an 'impact-ejecta-fallout' mechanism at the Greenland ice sheet are geological (0.65) and astronomical/cosmogenic (0.7), both comparatively high-detectability categories for this era, with material evidence (0.35) moderate and genetic (0.3), oral_tradition (0.1), iconographic (0.1), and linguistic (0.05) all weak or effectively unusable this far back (textual is 0.0, as writing did not exist). This is favorable: continuously drilled, well-dated Greenland ice cores (GISP2, NGRIP, NEEM) are exactly the kind of high-fidelity archive that should preserve a fallout signal (isotope spikes, spherules, PGE anomalies) if the event occurred, so absence of a confirmed signal would carry real evidentiary weight rather than being explained away by poor preservation. That said, the hypothesis itself is marked action='inconclusive', which is consistent with the real-world status of the broader Younger Dryas Impact Hypothesis: it remains actively and unresolved contested in the literature (proponents citing platinum/nanodiamond anomalies vs. critics disputing reproducibility and dating precision) — noted here only as a low-tier model-prior recollection, not verified against supplied evidence. Additionally, pairing 'supernova-event' as actor with an 'impact-ejecta-fallout' mechanism is an atypical combination in the literature I recall (most YD impact proposals invoke a cometary/asteroidal body, not a supernova specifically), which should be treated as a speculative variant rather than an established causal chain. Given the high detectability of the most relevant evidence classes (geological, astronomical) for this period, I suggest a detectability adjustment near 0.6, meaning any current absence of confirmed evidence is only partly attributable to poor survivability/detectability and partly weighs against the hypothesis's specific supernova mechanism.
